topic.coverageNote: Two open reviews were required: one on bone and joint tuberculosis and one on fungal arthritis. The ICU invasive-fungal consensus named in the spreadsheet is the wrong setting.

mcqs.question: In the bone-and-joint tuberculosis series, how long was the average time from symptom onset to diagnosis?

options.D: The paper does not report a delay

mcqs.explanation: The tuberculosis review says that, on average, the time from symptom onset to diagnosis was 6.1 months.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
sourceRefs.excerpt: the time from symptom onset to diagnosis was 6.1 months

mcqs.question: Which site was most often affected in that tuberculosis series?

options.C: Only the small joints of the hands
options.D: The paper found no dominant site

mcqs.explanation: Spinal tuberculosis was the most frequently affected site, accounting for 77.6% (700/902) of cases.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
sourceRefs.excerpt: Spinal tuberculosis was the most frequently affected site, accounting for 77.6% (700/902) of cases.

mcqs.question: What proportion of analysed M. tuberculosis strains were rifampicin-resistant in that paper?
mcqs.explanation: The paper reports rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis in 20.4% of analysed strains (95% CI 15.1–27.0%).

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

mcqs.question: What does the fungal-arthritis review require for a definitive diagnosis?

options.A: Bone or synovial culture or biopsy
options.D: Response to a single dose of fluconazole

mcqs.explanation: The fungal arthritis review says definitive diagnosis requires bone or synovial culture or biopsy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: definitive diagnosis requires bone or synovial culture or biopsy.

mcqs.question: How does the fungal-arthritis review describe treatment, and which organisms are most often reported?

options.A: Surgery plus prolonged antifungal therapy; Candida is most often reported, with Aspergillus also seen
options.B: A 5-day antibiotic course and no surgery
options.C: Only amphotericin, with azoles described as ineffective
options.D: Observation, because fungal arthritis is self-limited

mcqs.explanation: The review says Candida infections are mostly reported and Aspergillus also occurs. Diagnosis and management may involve multiple surgical interventions and prolonged antifungal therapy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Candida infections are mostly reported, but patients may also develop infections secondary to non- Candida fungi, especially Aspergillus . Diagnosis and management of these infections is challenging and may involve multiple surgical interventions and prolonged antifungal therapy.
